$comment: CANONICAL CONTRACT for bead sparkle-gazo4a — 'a monitor reports I COULD NOT SEE IT as IT IS NOT
THERE'. ONE file, read by the TypeScript suite AND by the Rust suite, so the two hand-written
halves cannot drift apart silently (AGENTS.md's `sparkle-16y6h` rule: share ONE fixture both
suites parse, so they fail TOGETHER).
A probe looks for something. The look FAILS — it errors, times out, lacks credentials, or comes
back empty from a query nobody proved was working — and the empty result is published as PROOF OF
ABSENCE rather than as a FAILED OBSERVATION. Every instance produces a confident wrong statement
that a human or another agent then acts on. Six are recorded below, all measured, all real.
EVERY PROBE REPORTS THREE OUTCOMES, NOT TWO:
FOUND          — we looked and it is there.
NOT-FOUND      — we looked, THE LOOK IS PROVEN TO WORK AND TO COVER THE GROUND THE CLAIM
COVERS, and it is not there. This outcome requires a CONTROL.
COULD-NOT-LOOK — anything else. The probe errored, timed out, lacked credentials, or returned
empty from a query whose reach was never established.
COULD-NOT-LOOK MUST NEVER RENDER AS ABSENCE, anywhere in the UI, in an alert, or in a prompt.
That is what `absenceClaims` below enforces: a phrase from that lexicon appearing in text
generated for a could-not-look outcome is the defect, and it is a test failure.
An empty result is only evidence of absence once you have shown the query can return a non-empty
one. The concierge established that `sparkle-reviewer` genuinely posts nothing by running
`gh repo view` ALONGSIDE the empty result — proving `gh` was authenticated and the repo
reachable. That one finding is reliable BECAUSE of the control; the five below are wrong because
nobody ran one.
A control has TWO halves and BOTH are required:
1. REACHABLE — the query mechanism works at all (authenticated, the host answered, the parse
succeeded). Without this, empty means 'the door was shut'.
2. COMPLETE  — the read covered the whole population the claim is about. A paginated, windowed,
or capped read PROVES PRESENCE BUT CAN NEVER PROVE ABSENCE: not seeing it settles nothing,
because it may live on a page nobody fetched. `ph_read_pool`'s third field in
scripts/lib/pipeline-health.sh is this same bit, and its comment records the measured victim.
A tri-state TYPE is necessary and is not sufficient: `HealthState::Unknown` has existed in
pipeline_health.rs the whole time, and four of the six instances below happened anyway — because
the DETAIL STRING attached to a correctly-typed reading still asserted absence in prose. The type
governs the fold; the lexicon governs the SENTENCE, which is the thing a human actually reads and
acts on. Both are needed.
The vocabulary of an ABSENCE CLAIM — case-insensitive regular expressions, in a syntax both
JavaScript's RegExp and Rust's `regex` crate accept unchanged (no lookaround, no backrefs).
APPLIED ONLY TO TEXT GENERATED FOR A could-not-look OUTCOME. A genuine NOT-FOUND is SUPPOSED to
say 'it is not there' — that is the whole point of the third outcome existing separately. So
these patterns are not banned words; they are words a could-not-look may not use.
Each entry names the measured instance whose real text it catches, so a future edit can tell a
pattern that is load-bearing from one that is decoration. `id` is referenced by `instances`.

patterns.caught: the ready-for-review label doesn't exist in the repo at all
there is no roborev daemon process
— not even a draft — so nothing is published
There is no release object at all for v0.140.0
no recent 'sparkle-reviewer' review was found and open PR(s) are waiting

patterns.re: \b(not found|no jobs found|no results found|nothing found)\b

patterns.caught: there is no roborev daemon process — the review daemon is not running
The PR reviewer (knightwatch) is unavailable — reprovision it
Nothing Sparkle can observe has changed since resume 2
the epic sweeper reading 'no observable change' as 'no progress'
Nobody is working on this epic right now

$comment: THE SIX MEASURED INSTANCES, converted into cases. Every one is driven through its REAL
production classifier or renderer by the suite named in `coveredBy` — never through a copy of
the mechanism, which is the vacuity shape AGENTS.md names (`guard-vacuity-relocates-upstream`).
`observation` is what the probe actually got back. `wrongClaim` is the sentence the shipped
code produced from it. `truth` is what was actually the case, established afterwards. A case
passes when the real code, fed `observation`, produces a could-not-look outcome AND text
carrying no pattern from `absenceClaims`.
`lang` picks which suite owns the case; `coveredBy` names the test. The COVERAGE GUARD in each
suite asserts every instance of its own language is claimed by a live test, so a case cannot be
quietly dropped — an instance list nobody runs is exactly the false-green this bead is about.

cases.observation: A repo-wide `issues/comments?per_page=100` read returned a FULL page (100 of 100) whose oldest comment is 15h old, and no comment in it carried the reviewer marker. The claim being made spans 48h.
cases.wrongClaim: the ready-for-review label doesn't exist in the repo at all
cases.truth: The label exists (colour #0E8A16, bead sparkle-x8fxcw). No OPEN PR carried it — a different fact with a different fix. Acting on the false version meant re-creating an existing label.
cases.mechanism: A capped page proves presence, never absence. The window (15h) is SHORTER than the claim (48h), so an empty read cannot settle the question and must report could-not-look.

cases.observation: The reviewer-liveness read came back with no reviewer comment in its window, while the open-PR read FAILED outright and was defaulted to false.
cases.wrongClaim: The PR reviewer (knightwatch) is unavailable — reprovision the VM.
cases.truth: Knightwatch was posting a real, substantive review on PR #2718 at that exact moment.
cases.mechanism: Two failed reads were each laundered into a negative fact — an unreadable comment window into 'no review', an unreadable PR list into 'no open PRs'. Neither is an observation.

cases.observation: An 8-second `roborev status` probe timed out, and no daemon evidence (process liveness, launchd state, store size, lock activity) could be read either.
cases.wrongClaim: there is no roborev daemon process — the review daemon is not running
cases.truth: The daemon was alive and answering in 0.5-0.9ms.
cases.mechanism: A timeout is a property of the OBSERVATION, not of the thing observed. With no corroborating evidence the only honest verdict is could-not-look.

cases.observation: A `gh api repos/<repo>/releases` read that could not be proven to include drafts returned no object for the newest tag.
cases.wrongClaim: There is no release object at all for v0.140.0 — not even a draft.
cases.truth: A draft existed. Drafts are visible only to a token with the right scope, so an under-scoped or truncated read sees a published-only view.
cases.mechanism: 'Not even a draft' is a claim about a population the read was never shown to cover. Without that proof it is could-not-look.

cases.observation: The sweeper compared two board readings and saw no difference in the fields it can see, while workers were actively committing to the epic's branches.
cases.truth: Workers were committing throughout. The sweeper's mark simply does not observe commits.
cases.mechanism: 'I cannot see this kind of progress' is not 'there is no progress'. An unchanged mark whose inputs do not cover the work in question is could-not-look.

cases.observation: An agent's progress mark did not move across two sweeps while it was running a long verify, or waiting on a queued CI run with no open PR yet to gate on.
cases.wrongClaim: Nothing Sparkle can observe has changed since resume 1.
cases.truth: The agent was working fine. A long verification run and a queued CI run both move nothing the mark reads.
cases.mechanism: The mark reads prompt history and tool activity; it does not read a running verify or a queued run. An unmoved mark under a known-unobservable wait is could-not-look, and re-arming on it interrupts working agents.

cases.observation: The epic sweep read its board from a beads snapshot that had not been refreshed for 2h20m. `beadsStore.refresh` KEEPS the previous snapshot when `bd` fails, writing only `error[projectId]`, and its poller is reference-counted on VIEWERS while this sweep exists to run on projects nobody is viewing. The read succeeded, parsed, and was complete — and described an earlier state of the store.
cases.wrongClaim: There is no sweep-restarted marker on this epic and no founder veto, so its one automatic restart is still owed.
cases.truth: The bead carried the founder's `no-auto-restart` veto and, by the end, FOURTEEN `sweep-restarted:` markers the sweep had written itself. Every one of them was in the store and none was in the snapshot.
cases.mechanism: Every brake on this sweep is a LABEL — the veto, the `sweep-restarted:` budget marker, the `stalled` escalation mark — so a snapshot predating those writes reports all three absent, which is exactly the state that authorizes a restart. It restarted one epic 14 times at a 601s cadence, wiping its agent's context each time, while its own notice promised it would stop. Its audit note carries the fingerprint: 'no child bead has moved in 16h', then 17h, 18h, 19h on successive ticks, because `now` advanced while `lastChildProgressAt` could not. A stale read is `complete: false` — the population read is not the population the claim is about — so `beadsObserved` is false and the sweep skips `beads-unknown` before reading any other field.

cases.observation: `babysit_leases` returned a readable list with NO row for this PR. The agent roster, which was never consulted, held a live babysit driver for it.
cases.wrongClaim: No agent is driving drodio/sparkle#74, so the lease is free and a driver may be dispatched.
cases.truth: A driver had owned that PR for two hours and was alive and visible on the roster the whole time. Four PRs ended up with two agents each; the duplicates could not even be retired, because by then they held uncommitted work on the branch their twin owned.
cases.mechanism: The lease store is not the population the claim is about. A driver started through the babysit SKILL, by a human, or by an orchestrator writes no lease at all — SKILL.md assumes the dispatcher took one on its behalf — so it is structurally invisible and the read comes back empty for a PR that is owned. Separately `babysit_lease_heartbeat` has NO frontend caller, so `heartbeat_at_ms` is stamped once at acquire and never refreshed and every live driver is reclassified `dead-stale` at 90 minutes. The roster answer is a tri-state (`processAliveFor`): observed-live holds, observed-exit releases, and NOT-OBSERVED holds rather than reading as absent.
